title: California bans AI-only firing decisions from July 2027
key_facts: California will bar employers from relying solely on automated decision systems to discipline or fire workers from 1 July 2027 under SB 947, by Senator Jerry McNerney.
Governor Gavin Newsom approved it on 30 Sep 2026; it was chaptered the same day as Chapter 859, Statutes of 2026.
Where an employer primarily relies on such a system, a human must corroborate the decision with other evidence, and the worker must get a plain-language written notice that software was involved.
If the output cannot be corroborated or the reviewer finds it inaccurate, incomplete or misleading, it may not be used for the decision.
Three uses are banned outright, including inferring protected status and predicting and acting against workers for exercising legal rights.
The Labor Commissioner enforces, with a civil penalty of $500 per violation; public prosecutors can also enforce.
The law does not define "primarily", leaving a gap for the Labor Commissioner or courts to fill.
quote_evidence: "An employer shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a disciplinary or termination decision," it states.
The law does not define "primarily," which leaves a gap that the Labor Commissioner or the courts will presumably have to fill.
why_it_matters_hint: A first-of-its-kind workplace limit on AI in firing decisions in the largest US state.
